newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ business confidence recovers in Sept qtr-NZIER.
newsitem.headline: NZ business confidence recovers in Sept qtr-NZIER.

text.p: New Zealand business confidence recovered lost ground in the September quarter, according to a survey published by the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research on Friday.
However, the institute noted the pessimists still outweigh the optimists.

The NZIER's Quarterly Survey of Business Opinion showed that in the September quarter, a net one percent of businesses surveyed expected a deterioration in the general business situation during the next six months.
This compared with a net 34 percent in the June quarter survey who expected conditions to get worse.

Pessimists still outweighed optimists in manufacturing and building, but in the wholesale and retail sectors they were perfectly balanced. In the service sector, optimists now outweighed those expecting a general decline in the business situation.
"Coupled with the increased confidence of service firms are expectations of lower interest rates. This appears to have buoyed many firms," NZIER said.
A net 48 percent of financial service firms expected interest rates to fall over the next twelve months compared to a net 38 percent expecting interest rate rises last quarter.
All sectors expected increases in new orders and domestic sales over the next three months.
"However, the tax cuts appear not to have had any real effect yet, with domestic sales falling in all sectors in the September quarter," NZIER said.

"Moreover, the high exchange rate has finally affected manufactured exports. For the first time in eight years, the number of manufacturers reporting a decline in export sales outweigh those reporting an increase."
According to the survey, employment and overtime have fallen. Average costs increased for the 11th consecutive quarter, possibly driven by increasing wages.
"Wage increases appear to be contributing to rising costs, suggesting that inflationary pressures still persist. However prices, as measured in the survey, largely remained static," NZIER said.
It said the squeeze between costs and prices had resulted in a further decline in profitability in all sectors during the quarter.
"Yet, overall, confidence appears to be returning, reflecting expectations of lower interst rates and rises in new orders and sales."
